Subject: Initial questions on BAA, PHI handling and phased onboarding

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week. St. Jude Health is evaluating Redwood for a phased rollout where a small set of clinicians will start using an assistant to transcribe consult notes and surface insights. Before we proceed we'd like to confirm a few items that will determine whether we can sign a BAA and proceed with a pilot:

- Can Redwood act as a Business Associate under our BAA for a phased pilot (initially ~50 clinicians) and then scale?
- For streaming transcription (real-time speech->text), does Redwood persist audio or transcripts by default? If not, what optional retention exists and how is it controlled?
- Do logs / traces contain PHI? What is retained in audit logs and how long?
- Are there deployment options that isolate PHI (dedicated or private)? Our security team prefers VPC + customer-managed keys when PHI is involved.
- We also need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short DPIA summary.

Attached is our questionnaire (we filled the first pass) and a simple data flow diagram for the pilot. Can your team confirm these items and propose next steps? Procurement wants to understand the minimum scope required in the BAA for a pilot.

Best,
Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in our legal and product leads to make sure we give precise answers. Quick summary up front: yes — we can sign a BAA and support a phased pilot with options for dedicated/private deployments. Details below and a few clarifying Qs so we scope the BAA correctly.

Questions for St. Jude:
- Will audio be sent to Redwood for transcription, or will you pre-process on-prem and send text only?
- Is the pilot limited to U.S.-resident patients? (affects regional controls and retention)
- Do you require audit logs to be retained longer than our standard 90-day window for pilot telemetry?

High-level answers (we'll provide formal artifacts):
- BAA: Redwood has a standard BAA for HIPAA-compliant customers. It can be scoped to pilot-specific systems and truncated timelines for staged onboarding.
- Transcription storage: By default hosted streaming is ephemeral — audio and generated text are not written to long-term storage unless explicitly enabled by the customer. We log metadata for debugging (non-content), and we can configure logs/audit retention.
- PHI in logs: We separate content vs telemetry. Content (transcripts) is only stored if customer enables persistence; when enabled, it can be placed in a dedicated tenant with controlled retention. Audit traces may contain identifiers if enabled; we have a configurable redaction pipeline.
- Deployment options: Hosted with customer-configurable retention, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + tenant isolation), Private (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM — all supported. Private deployments meet your VPC + CMK preference.

I'll follow up with a short write-up and the SOC 2 and DPIA artifacts. Laura — can you draft a BAA scope for a 3-month pilot that limits content persistence to "off" by default and enumerates permitted processing? Dev — can you confirm streaming retention defaults and redaction controls? Monica — can you propose an onboarding checklist for St. Jude?

Thanks,
Rafael

Thanks Rafael — drafting language now. Notes for the BAA draft and engagement:

- Scope approach: create a pilot appendix specifying (a) pilot duration (90 days), (b) datasets/environments included (pilot-tenant), (c) permitted processing (real-time transcription, no persistent storage unless customer opt-in), and (d) personnel/access restrictions.
- Minimum required controls to list: SOC 2 Type II evidence, encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+), at-rest encryption (AES-256) for persisted content, KMS integration for Private, MFA for console access, role-based access with principle of least privilege.
- Audit logs: default retention 90 days; for pilot we can extend to 1 year on request but will require a separate data retention addendum.
- DPIA: we'll provide a 1-page DPIA summary that maps data flows to risk mitigations (encryption, pseudonymization, access controls, logging).

Draft action items:
1) Rafael: send customer-facing summary and next steps.
2) Dev: confirm streaming pipeline behavior (ephemeral vs persisted) and how redaction works (pre-tokenization vs post).
3) Monica: onboarding checklist and a short runbook for canary launch.

I'll attach a BAA appendix template and suggested pilot wording.

Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: Initial questions on BAA, PHI handling and phased onboarding (technical clarity)

Quick technical summary for the thread:

- Streaming transcription: hosted streaming uses an ephemeral in-memory pipeline. By default neither raw audio nor full transcripts are persisted to object storage. We do buffer tokens in RAM and maintain KV caches for model context; those are ephemeral and cleared per session unless the customer enables transcript persistence.
- Persistence options: customers can opt to persist transcripts to their tenant storage (encrypted at rest). When enabled, transcripts are stored in an isolated namespace and can be set to TTL (30/90/365 days).
- Logs & traces: service logs capture events and request metadata (timestamps, request IDs, model metrics). We do not record full transcript text in standard request logs. We can enable PII redaction in the processing pipeline (regex + model-assisted redaction) before logs are written.
- Dedicated / Private: Dedicated (reserved pools) gives tenant isolation but uses Redwood's managed infra; Private (VPC or on-prem) allows customer-managed KMS and network isolation. For HIPAA pilot we recommend Private or Dedicated with a dedicated tenant and CMK if St. Jude insists on customer key control.
- SOC 2 & DPIA: SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; DPIA summary will be compiled and sent.

Happy to join a technical call to walk through the pipeline with St. Jude infra/security.

– Dev Patel

Hi Elena — thanks for the details and the patience while we gathered internal inputs. Below is a concise summary and proposed next steps for the pilot BAA and onboarding. Please let us know if you want any of this adjusted before we prepare formal documents.

Summary for St. Jude Pilot:
- BAA: Redwood will execute our standard BAA with a pilot appendix that limits scope to a tenant named stjude-pilot, pilot duration 90 days, and permitted processing: real-time transcription and analysis only. The appendix will explicitly state that transcript persistence is OFF by default.
- Deployment & keys: For maximum isolation we recommend Private (VPC) with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). As an alternative, Dedicated reserved capacity + tenant isolation is acceptable; Redwood will enable encryption-at-rest with our KMS and can integrate with your KMS via cross-account keys.
- Data retention & logs: Default telemetry/audit retention is 90 days; we can extend to 1 year with a retention addendum. Standard logs do not contain full transcript content; we can enable redaction on any logs/metrics that might capture identifiers.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report and a 1-page DPIA summary will be provided under NDA.
- Operational: Redwood will deliver an onboarding checklist and runbook, and offer a technical deep-dive call with our infra team.

Next steps we propose:
1) St. Jude confirms whether audio will be sent raw to Redwood or if you will preprocess on-prem.
2) Sign a mutual NDA (if not already in place) so we can share SOC 2 artifacts and the DPIA.
3) Redwood sends BAA pilot appendix + short DPIA summary for review (ETA 2 business days).
4) Schedule a 45-minute technical call with your security/infra and our infra/product team (Dev + infra) — we have availability Wed/Thu next week.

I've attached the filled questionnaire with inline notes and the data flow diagram annotated. If you want an initial minimal BAA with only the pilot systems scoped, we can provide that and iterate.

Best regards,
